title: Avoid Illusions of Knowing
heading: Avoid Illusions of Knowing
coreClaim: The chapter argues that familiarity and repeated exposure can create an illusion of knowing, while honest calibration requires retrieval, explanation, delayed checks, and objective feedback.
distinctMechanism: The mechanism is calibration: forcing knowledge to stand on its own rather than borrowing confidence from recognition on the page.
requiredAnchors: Familiarity is not the same as durable knowledge.
Rereading and highlighting can inflate confidence without proving recall.
Honest checks require retrieval, explanation, or transfer.
commonMisreadings: Passive review alone can certify learning.
specificApplications: Replace one reread with closed-book explanation.
Use delayed self-quizzes to judge retention.
Ask for explanation or transfer before calling the material learned.
hardEdgeRequirement: Keep subjective confidence and demonstrated knowledge clearly separated.
thresholdQuestion: What kind of check forces knowledge to stand on its own instead of leaning on recognition?
